title: Gambling
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Betting is common around many learners (phones, football). Avoid naming real betting companies. A learner whose family is affected is never singled out.

skills.key_step: The learner identifies types of gambling in Kenya (sports betting, lotteries, casinos, card games for money), discusses causes (wish for quick money, peer pressure, adverts, idleness, poverty) and examines effects on individuals and families (debt, theft, quarrels, school drop-out, addiction).

floor.prerequisite: Knows good and poor uses of leisure.
floor.question: Which is a good use of free time: gambling or reading?

steps: Examine effects on self and family.
contexts: a family without food money after betting

board.do: Draw three columns: type, cause, effect.
Point at "sports betting on a phone".
board.say: Name a cause and an effect.

board.do: Wait for the learner to answer.

listen_for: Playing cards for money with friends is just a game
misconceptions.repair: List types in Kenya: sports betting on phones, lotteries, casinos, card games for money, pool for money.

misconceptions.ask: Which is an effect of gambling?
misconceptions.repair: Show the maths: most players lose. List effects on the gambler and family.
Read 1 Timothy 6:10 in full and underline "the love of".

misconceptions.ask: Kip places one small bet with his pocket money and wins. What is the danger?
misconceptions.repair: Discuss how habits begin; read 1 Corinthians 6:12: "I will not be mastered by anything".

checks.question: Which is gambling: farming or betting on a game?
Name an effect of gambling on a family.

skills.key_step: The learner outlines the scriptures on money and true riches: love of money is the danger (1 Timothy 6:10); honest money grows little by little (Proverbs 13:11); haste to be rich brings trouble (Proverbs 28:20-22); work honestly and share (Ephesians 4:28); be content (Hebrews 13:5); store treasures in heaven by good deeds (Matthew 6:19-21; 1 Timothy 6:17-19).

floor.question: Name one effect of gambling on a family.

representations: verse cards with a key phrase each
two columns: earthly riches, true riches
a savings chart: little by little against one bet
contexts: a betting advert on a phone
a youth who wins once and loses more

board.do: Draw two columns: earthly riches and true riches.
Point at the card "generous to the needy".
board.say: Which column, and which verse says so?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say true riches, 1 Timothy 6:18.
Fill in both columns from the verses.

misconceptions.ask: What does 1 Timothy 6:10 say is a root of all kinds of evil?
misconceptions.repair: Read the whole verse and underline "the love of". Money can be used well; loving it is the danger.

listen_for: It is too slow and wasted effort
misconceptions.ask: What does Proverbs 13:11 say about money gathered little by little?
misconceptions.repair: Compare two savers on a chart: little by little each week against one big bet. Read Proverbs 28:20.

listen_for: Money kept safe in a bank
misconceptions.ask: What are treasures in heaven, in Matthew 6:19-21?
misconceptions.repair: Read 1 Timothy 6:18 beside Matthew 6:20: be rich in good deeds, generous and willing to share.

misconceptions.ask: According to Ephesians 4:28, what should a former thief do?
misconceptions.repair: Read Ephesians 4:28 in three parts and write them as three steps.

checks.question: What are treasures in heaven?
checks.answer: Good deeds and a life given to God
